settings.name_in_paper: Contextual combinatorial (semi-)bandit with unknown score function h (CN-UCB analysis)
unmapped: Score of arm i at round t is h(x_{t,i}) + noise with unknown h in [0,1]; contexts x_{t,i} observed each round (no stated generation process)
Reward R(S, v) is an unknown deterministic function of the scores, monotone and Lipschitz (constant C_0) in the scores of S; learner has an exact argmax oracle over super arms
S here is the learner's bound B >= sqrt(2 h^T H^{-1} h) on the NTK-RKHS norm of h
NTK matrix H on all T*K contexts satisfies H >= lambda_0 I; contexts have unit norm and symmetric halves
settings.definition_quote: At round $t \in [\TotalRound]$, a learning agent observes the set of context vectors for all arms $\{ \mathbf{x}_{t, i} \in \mathbb{R}^d \mid i \in [\TotalAction] \}$ and chooses a set of arms $S_t \subset [N]$ with size constraint $|S_t| = K$. ... $\Score_{t, i} = h(\mathbf{x}_{t,i}) + \Noise_{t,i}$ where $h$ is an unknown function satisfying $0 \le h(\mathbf{x}) \le 1$ ... and $\Noise_{t,i}$ is a $\SubGaussian$-sub-Gaussian noise satisfying $\mathbb{E}[\Noise_{t,i}| \mathcal{F}_t] = 0$

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual combinatorial (semi-)bandit with unknown score function h (CN-TS analysis)
unmapped: Score of arm i at round t is h(x_{t,i}) + noise with unknown h in [0,1]; contexts observed each round (no stated generation process)
Reward R(S, v) is an unknown deterministic function of the scores, monotone and Lipschitz (constant C_0); learner has an exact argmax oracle over super arms
S here is the norm parameter B (bound on the NTK-RKHS norm of h) used in the exploration variance nu
NTK matrix H on all T*K contexts satisfies H >= lambda_0 I; contexts have unit norm and symmetric halves
settings.definition_quote: At round $t \in [\TotalRound]$, a learning agent observes the set of context vectors for all arms ... and chooses a set of arms $S_t \subset [N]$ with size constraint $|S_t| = K$. ... $\Score_{t, i} = h(\mathbf{x}_{t,i}) + \Noise_{t,i}$

symbols.C_0: Lipschitz constant of the reward in the scores

conditions: Assumption 1: reward monotone non-decreasing in scores
Assumption 2: reward Lipschitz in scores of S with constant C_0
Assumption 3: ||x||_2 = 1, symmetric context halves, NTK matrix H >= lambda_0 I
tuning: m_width >= poly(T, L, N, lambda^{-1}, lambda_0^{-1}, log T)
eta = C1 (T K m L + m lambda)^{-1}
J = 2 log(sqrt(lambda/TK)/(lambda + C3 T K L)) T K L/(C1 lambda) gradient steps

source.label: thm_CN-UCB
source.quote: Suppose Assumptions~\ref{assum:monotone}-\ref{assum:context} hold. ... If we run $\CNUCB$ with $m \ge poly(T, L, N, \lambda^{-1}, \lambda_0^{-1}, \log T)$, ... then the cumulative expected regret of $\CNUCB$ over horizon~$T$ is upper-bounded by $\Rcal(T) = \tilde{\Ocal}\left( \sqrt{ \tilde{d} T \max\{ \tilde{d}, K\} }\right)$.

results.notes: Paper's K (super-arm size) mapped to m, paper's N (number of arms) to K, effective dimension d_tilde to d_eff. Regret defined via expected scores: pseudo-regret against per-round optimal super arm. Appendix gives informal extensions to alpha-approximation oracle (alpha-regret same order) and unknown T via doubling (CN-UCB-D), not formal statements. Compute polynomial per round given the oracle.

symbols.C_0: Lipschitz constant of the reward in the scores

conditions: Assumption 1: reward monotone non-decreasing in scores
Assumption 2: reward Lipschitz in scores of S
Assumption 3: ||x||_2 = 1, symmetric context halves, NTK matrix H >= lambda_0 I
tuning: nu = B + sigma sqrt(d_tilde log(1+TN/lambda) + 2 + 2 log T)
B = max{1/(22 e sqrt(pi)), sqrt(2 h^T H h)}
M = ceil(1 - log K / log(1 - p_tilde)) samples per arm, p_tilde = 1/(4 e sqrt(pi))

source.label: thm_CN-TS
source.quote: Suppose Assumptions~\ref{assum:monotone}-\ref{assum:context} hold and $\NetworkWidth$ satisfies Condition~\ref{cond_network width}. If we run \texttt{CN-TS} with ... then the cumulative expected regret of \texttt{CN-TS} over horizon~$T$ is upper-bounded by $\Rcal (T) = \tilde{\Ocal}( \tilde{d} \sqrt{T K})$.

results.notes: Paper's K -> m, N -> K, d_tilde -> d_eff. Worst-case (frequentist) regret. Exploration variance nu uses d_eff, so learner knows d_eff (or bound). Informal appendix extensions to alpha-approx oracle and unknown T (CN-TS-D) give same order.
